title: Ops reliability guerrilla tests and runbook scratchpad
content:
Purpose
Quick, low-friction experiments to validate SLO ownership boundaries, escalation shorthand, and minimal runbook actions for emerging production failure modes. This doc is intentionally messy — a scratchpad for ops-led "guerrilla" reliability tests we can run with partner teams (hosted-api, runtime, console).

High-level goals
- Validate that 2-minute triage scripts reduce MTTR for transient model-slow events by >30% in a controlled blast window.
- Exercise cross-team escalation: primary oncall -> model-owner -> infra -> SRE runbook within 15 minutes.
- Verify automated fallback routing triggers when per-model latency 95p breaches configured SLO for 3 continuous minutes.
- Confirm runbook play is readable and executable by non-SRE engineer in an emergency.

Who to invite / quick availability
- Minimum crew: oncall eng (hosted-api), model-owner (runtime), infra ops, SRE pair. (4 people)
- Run length: 45 min (30m test + 15m debrief)
- Slack bridge channel: #reliability-guerilla (create ephemeral thread: topic: guerilla/test-<date>)

Experiment catalog (short form)
1) Latency spike, model queue backlog (cheap synthetic)
- Trigger: synthetic load from canary runner hitting model-X with 4x normal token velocity for 10 min.
- Observables: route-level p95 latency, serving queue depth metric, request_shed_count.
- Runbook extract (quick):
  * Step 1 (2m): Enable verbose tracing on model-X (toggle via /internal/debug/trace?model=model-X)
  * Step 2 (3m): If queue_depth>50 and p95>1200ms, flip traffic to model-X-fallback variant (route: r1 -> model-X-quantized).
  * Step 3 (5m): If fallback reduces p95 by >=20% confirm and mark incident as mitigated; otherwise escalate to infra.
- Success criteria: fallback reduces p95 by >=20% within 5 minutes.

2) KV cache corruption simulation (read-only glitch)
- Trigger: inject malformed prefix in canary cache via test harness (read-only simulate mismatch).
- Observables: cache_hit_rate drop, increased token compute, error rate of decoder aligners.
- Quick mitigation: flush per-model prefix cache and force cold-start for a small subset (10% traffic).
- Post-test: measure cold-start penalty and decide threshold for autoflush policy.

3) Canary routing misconfiguration (human error scenario)
- Trigger: push controlled misroute (route weight swap 5% -> 95%) using CI toggle during maintenance window.
- Observables: unexpected model variant serving and user-visible hallucination rate (synthetic evals), user request latency.
- Runbook snippet: roll-back route toggle, open postmortem note in Jira, notify customer-facing channel.

Operational checklist (for the run)
- Pre-test (24h): notify SRE, runtime, console slack channels. Create temporary incident stub in Jira: JIRA-GUERILLA-<date>.
- Pre-test (1h): confirm canary runner healthy, monitoring dashboards loaded, pager coverage OK.
- During: one person assigned to "scribe" and capture metrics/links; one person to watch dashboards; one person executes runbook steps.
- Post-test (15m): capture result, update the runbook doc, assign follow-ups (who will update runbook text, who will file bug, who will create rollouts).

Runbook usability heuristics (what we check quickly)
- Is the runbook actionable with 3 lines max per mitigation step? (Y/N)
- Can a non-SRE complete first two steps without elevated permissions? (Y/N)
- Does the doc state clear rollback triggers and SLAs for re-enabling default routes? (Y/N)

Quick metrics to capture (minimum)
- p95 latency (route/model)
- queue_depth
- fallback_traffic_percent
- incident_duration_minutes
- customer_error_rate / user-visible failures per 1k reqs

Communication templates (short, copy-ready)
- Pre-test notice: "Heads up: running controlled reliability test against model-X at HH:MM UTC on DATE. Expect short latency increases for 5-10% traffic. No action required unless paged."
- Post-test summary: "Guerilla test result: fallback reduced p95 by 26%; KV flush required; follow-ups: runtime to add auto-flush threshold; infra to investigate cache checksum drift. Detailed notes: <link>"

Open questions / risks (notes to follow up)
- Are any customers pinned to specific model variants that would be harmed by traffic toggles? (inventory check)
- Permissions: can first-responder non-SRE safely flip traffic? need a temporary RBAC shortcut for tests.
- Observability gaps: we lack a single panel that shows model_x queue_depth + fallback_share + p95 in one view. Quick dashboard ask -> observability team.

Follow-ups & owners (immediate)
- Create ephemeral dashboard: Lena Sorensen (action) — due +3 days.
- RBAC test permissions for runbook toggles: Ravi Patel — due +7 days.
- Draft improved runbook text (make it 3-line actionable): Maya Chen + Aisha Kapoor — due +2 days.

Notes-to-self / scratch fragments (raw)
- consider a "minimally intrusive" mode: run fallback on 1% traffic for longer window to gather signal without big user impact.
- test window idea: stagger 5m on / 10m off cycles to window effects.
- include a tiny script for autogenerating incident stub to reduce friction.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets (for run)
- enable tracing: curl -X POST https://internal-admin.redwood/api/v1/debug/trace?model=model-X -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- flip route weight: curl -X POST https://internal-config/redwood/routes/set-weight -d '{"route":"r1","model":"model-X-fallback","weight":0.2}'
- flush prefix cache: curl -X POST https://internal-cache/flush?prefix=model-X-abc

End of scratchpad — this doc should turn awkward test steps into a repeatable recipe. After 2-3 runs we can formalize into the SLO playbook proper.

Version history (short)
- 2026-05-12: created (Maya Chen)
- 2026-05-20: first draft checklist edits (Ravi Patel)
- 2026-06-03: added CLI snippets and owners (Lena Sorensen)
